gates.proposition: South Base triangulation station existed by the 1904 magnetic occupation referenced in the 1908 and 1909 C&GS station descriptions.
evidence: 1908 C&GS magnetic station description states the 1904 station was reoccupied between Morro Lighthouse and South Base triangulation station, 20 paces from South Base.
1909 C&GS report states observations were made 50 feet from South Base triangulation station toward Morro Lighthouse, within a few feet of the 1904/1908 point.
gates.effect: Existence by 1904 is verified. This does not establish the original construction/occupation year.

gates.proposition: South Base triangulation station is not the 1904/1908 magnetic observation point and is not the separately monumented 1909 magnetic station.
evidence: The magnetic point is described by offset from South Base.
The 1909 point was independently monumented with a cement stone marked U.S.C.&G.S., 1909.
gates.effect: Never transfer a magnetic-station coordinate/mark to South Base without an explicit tie computation.

gates.proposition: The true bearing from the South Base vicinity toward Morro Lighthouse was N 37°09.4′ E.
gates.evidence: C&GS 1909 magnetic station description says the bearing was determined from triangulation.
gates.effect: Provides an orientation constraint but not a unique coordinate.

gates.proposition: The current official NGS positions for SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE (TV1051) and MORRO LIGHTHOUSE (TV1029) reproduce the 1909 C&GS South Base→Morro lighthouse bearing to within about 9 arcseconds.
limits: This is an independent identity/topology diagnostic, not a substitute for original 1899/1909 observation reductions.

The lighthouse underwent historical structural changes; the calculation uses the official NGS station MORRO LIGHTHOUSE TV1029 and therefore must not be generalized to every lighthouse epoch without a station-history tie.
gates.effect: Strongly corroborates that TV1051 is the historical South Base referenced by the 1909 magnetic description.

gates.proposition: Hodgkins surveyed San Juan Harbor in April 1899; official NGS station histories independently preserve an 1899 C&GS/WCH San Juan control layer including SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE, SAN JUAN NORTH BASE and MORRO CASTLE.
limits: The 1898-99 annual report itself describes the San Juan harbor survey but does not name South Base.
The station-name/date identity comes from the official NGS datasheet archive, not from wording in the annual report.
The original GB/GBZ measured-base record is still required before calling the North↔South line a formally measured baseline with a specific historical length/method.
gates.effect: The 1899 local-control branch is no longer merely plausible: an 1899 C&GS station network at San Juan is verified. Formal base-measurement details remain open.

gates.proposition: Stehman Forney led triangulation from Ponce to San Juan Jan-May 1900; NGS independently records MORRO CASTLE 2 as a 1900 CGS station described by (SF) and MORRO LIGHTHOUSE as first observed by CGS in 1900.
limits: This does not yet prove that Forney/SF occupied TV1051 South Base.

model: 1899: SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE (TV1051) monumented by CGS and described by C&GS 1899 (WCH) — verified.
1899: SAN JUAN NORTH BASE (TV1049) monumented by CGS and described by C&GS 1899 (WCH) — verified.

1901: TV1051 recovered GOOD by CGS; a 20-foot tripod and scaffold signal was erected over the station.
1904: South Base used as a triangulation reference for magnetic work — independently verified.
gates.effect: The former hypothesis that South Base may have originated in 1900 is superseded by official NGS station history: the monument existed in 1899. The unresolved question is now the exact 1899 survey operation/base measurement and the role of Forney's 1900 campaign.
